full_judgment: 2. The short facts which have given rise to the Rule are as follows:- The plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 32 of 1973 for declaration of title to the suit land described in the schedule of the plaint and recovery of khas possession thereto in alternate for awarding a money decree of Taka 10,175.10 being the compensation award for the suit land which has been requisitioned by the government for fish seed multiplication farm at Khatlal; that the jotes appertaining to CS Khatian Nos. 385, 718, 1063, 1269 and 1655 of Mouza Khatlal under PS Khetlal, District Bogra belonged to Horekrishna Nath and Ramkrishna Nath in equal share; that the same were recorded in their names correctly in .CS operation; that the said maleks entered into amicable partition of their aforesaid properties after CS operation and in consequence thereof the Ka schedule land measuring 1.72 and 1/2 decimals fell exclusively in the saham of Horekrishna Nath who being in possession thereto died leaving a son Krishna Debnath and a daughter Ananda Sundary; that Sree Krishna Devnath married one Joyananda Sundary and they had no issue, that the Sree Krishna Devnath purchased the 'Kha' schedule property measuring 49 and 1/2 decimals 2 along with other lands in the benami of his wife and since purchase he used to possess the 'Kha' schedule land in his own right, title and interest and that Sree Krishna Devnath being in exclusive possession over the Ka and Kha schedule lands and his wife Jayananda Sundry died. It is further stated that the plaintiffs are sons of Ananda Sundry, the full sister of Sree Krishna Devnath and, as such, they inherited the suit lands along with other properties left by Sree Krishna Devnath as his legal heirs and since then they used to possess the same in their own right, title and interest; that on 15th Ashar 1374 BS corresponding to 30-7-67 AD, the local Tahshildar of Khatlal threatened the Bargadars of the plaintiffs to dispossess therefrom on the plea that the properties left by Sree Krishna Devnath were taken overby the government as he left no heirs and that the plain- tiffs are not legal heirs of the deceased Sree Krishna Devnath.
